details: picklescan before 0.0.22 only considers standard pickle file extensions in the scope for its vulnerability scan. An attacker could craft a malicious model that uses Pickle and include a malicious pickle file with a non-standard file extension. Because the malicious pickle file inclusion is not considered as part of the scope of picklescan, the file would pass security checks and appear to be safe, when it could instead prove to be problematic.

A vulnerability in the GraphCypherQAChain class of langchain-ai/langchain-community version 0.2.5 allows for SQL injection through prompt injection. This vulnerability can lead to unauthorized data manipulation, data exfiltration, denial of service (DoS) by deleting all data, breaches in multi-tenant security environments, and data integrity issues. Attackers can create, update, or delete nodes and relationships without proper authorization, extract sensitive data, disrupt services, access data across different tenants, and compromise the integrity of the database.

cna.title: Newsletter < 9.4.0 - Unauthenticated Unconfirmed Subscriber Takeover via Re-subscription Token Disclosure

descriptions.value: The Newsletter  WordPress plugin before 9.4.0 does not keep a subscriber's secret key out of the redirect it returns after a subscription request when double opt-in is enabled, allowing unauthenticated attackers to confirm a subscription for any email address without access to its mailbox and, when the address already has an unconfirmed subscription, to reset that record with their own details.

cna.title: RSVPMaker for Toastmasters < 6.9.3 - Reflected XSS via app Parameter

descriptions.value: The RSVPMaker for Toastmasters WordPress plugin before 6.9.3 does not sanitise and escape a parameter before outputting it back in an admin page, leading to a Reflected Cross-Site Scripting which could be used against high privilege users such as admin.

cna.title: Titan Anti-spam & Security < 7.5.5 - Unauthenticated Diagnostic Archive Disclosure

descriptions.value: The Titan Anti-spam & Security  WordPress plugin before 7.5.5 does not protect or remove the diagnostic archive it writes to the uploads folder when an administrator exports its logs, and names it after the export date alone, allowing unauthenticated visitors to download the Titan Anti-spam & Security  WordPress plugin before 7.5.5's logs, including visitor IP addresses, and the site's system information.

cna.title: Keywords to Links Converter < 2.2.5 - Subscriber+ Persistent Denial of Service

descriptions.value: The Keywords to Links Converter WordPress plugin before 2.2.5 does not validate a value submitted to one of its AJAX actions before saving it as an option that it later uses in an arithmetic operation on every admin and front-end request, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to make the whole site return a fatal error until the option is manually reset.

cna.title: FluentCommunity < 2.8.0 - Course Creator+ Cross-Course Lesson Relocation via IDOR

descriptions.description: CWE-639 Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

descriptions.value: The FluentCommunity  WordPress plugin before 2.8.0 does not check that a lesson belongs to the course a course creator is authorised to manage before moving it, allowing a user with the Course Creator role to move lessons out of other creators' courses into their own and read their content.

cna.title: Keywords to Links Converter 2.0.0 - 2.2.4 - Subscriber+ SQL Injection

descriptions.value: The Keywords to Links Converter WordPress plugin before 2.2.5 does not sanitise and escape a parameter before using it in a SQL statement via an AJAX action available to any authenticated user, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to perform SQL injection attacks and read arbitrary data from the database.

cna.title: FluentCommunity < 2.13.0 - Subscriber+ Cross-Owner Media Deletion via IDOR

descriptions.description: CWE-639 Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

descriptions.value: The FluentCommunity  WordPress plugin before 2.13.0 does not verify that a referenced media item belongs to the user, or is not already attached elsewhere, before re-linking it to their own content, and its media identifiers are predictable from public post data, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to take over and delete media uploaded by other users, including administrators.

cna.title: FluentCommunity < 2.7.0 - Space Admin+ Arbitrary Space Deletion and Modification via IDOR

descriptions.description: CWE-639 Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

descriptions.value: The FluentCommunity  WordPress plugin before 2.7.0 does not verify that the user is allowed to manage the space it actually modifies or deletes, allowing a user who administers any one space to modify or permanently delete any other space on the site, together with its posts, comments, reactions and memberships.

cna.title: FluentCommunity < 2.13.0 - Unauthenticated Restricted Space Link Disclosure

descriptions.value: The FluentCommunity  WordPress plugin before 2.13.0 does not apply the per-link visibility rules of space sidebar links when listing spaces in its space discovery feature, allowing unauthenticated visitors to retrieve the titles and URLs of links restricted to logged-in users or specific memberships, as well as disabled links, for every public and private space.

cna.title: Shortcodes Ultimate < 7.9.1 - Contributor+ Stored XSS via su_lightbox Shortcode

descriptions.value: The Shortcodes Ultimate  WordPress plugin before 7.9.1 does not restrict the content type of its lightbox shortcode, allowing users with the contributor role and above to make the lightbox fetch HTML from an attacker-controlled server and insert it into the page unsanitised, leading to Stored Cross-Site Scripting when a user opens the lightbox.

cna.title: Shortcodes Ultimate < 7.9.1 - Contributor+ SQLi via su_user and su_posts Shortcodes

descriptions.value: The Shortcodes Ultimate  WordPress plugin before 7.9.1 does not restrict which PHP functions a shortcode's filter attribute can call, allowing users with a role as low as Contributor to remove WordPress' term-slug sanitization and perform SQL injection attacks through another shortcode's taxonomy term attribute.

cna.title: Shortcodes Ultimate < 7.9.1 - Contributor+ Stored XSS via su_feed Shortcode

descriptions.value: The Shortcodes Ultimate  WordPress plugin before 7.9.1 does not escape the error message returned when a remote feed cannot be retrieved before outputting it, which could allow users with the contributor role and above to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks against administrators by pointing the feed at a server they control.

cna.title: Shortcodes Ultimate < 7.9.1 - Contributor+ Stored XSS via su_tooltip Shortcode

descriptions.value: The Shortcodes Ultimate  WordPress plugin before 7.9.1 does not prevent placeholders in a shortcode attribute from being expanded with unescaped nested shortcode output, allowing users with a role as low as contributor to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks.

cna.title: Shortcodes Ultimate < 7.9.1 - Contributor+ Stored XSS via su_menu Shortcode

descriptions.value: The Shortcodes Ultimate  WordPress plugin before 7.9.1 does not prevent format specifiers in a shortcode attribute from being interpreted when building navigation menu markup, which could allow users with a role as low as Contributor to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks.

cna.title: GetPaid 2.6.2 - 2.8.62 - Unauthenticated Invoice Disclosure via Payment Form Embed

descriptions.description: CWE-639 Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

affected.product: Payment forms, Buy now buttons, and Invoicing System | GetPaid

descriptions.value: The Payment forms, Buy now buttons, and Invoicing System | GetPaid WordPress plugin before 2.8.63 does not check that the visitor is allowed to view an invoice before rendering it through its single-invoice shortcode, and its payment-form embed page lets unauthenticated users render that shortcode for any invoice ID, disclosing customers' names, billing addresses, phone numbers, line items and payment status.

cna.title: Newsletter 9.1.1 - 9.3.9 - Subscriber Unsubscription via CSRF

descriptions.value: The Newsletter  WordPress plugin before 9.4.0 does not protect its unsubscription actions against Cross-Site Request Forgery for subscribers it identifies from its own tracking cookie, allowing attackers to unsubscribe a subscriber from the site's newsletter by making them visit a malicious page.

cna.title: Newsletter < 9.4.0 - Unauthenticated Open Redirect via 'redirect' Parameter

descriptions.description: CWE-601 URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

descriptions.value: The Newsletter  WordPress plugin before 9.4.0 does not properly validate the destination of the redirect performed when a subscriber changes their list membership from a newsletter link, checking only that it begins with the site's URL, allowing unauthenticated attackers to redirect users to external sites whose address starts with the site's URL.

cna.title: Newsletter < 9.4.0 - Unauthenticated Private Newsletter Disclosure via Subscriber Email

descriptions.value: The Newsletter  WordPress plugin before 9.4.0 does not check that a visitor is really the subscriber before showing them newsletters marked as private, and accepts a weaker subscriber identifier that anyone can obtain by submitting a known subscriber's email address to the public subscription form, allowing unauthenticated attackers who know a subscriber's email address to read every private newsletter sent to that subscriber.

cna.title: RSVP and Event Management < 2.7.19 - Reflected XSS via 'rsvp_note' Parameter

descriptions.value: The RSVP and Event Management WordPress plugin before 2.7.19 does not escape a submitted value before outputting it back in its RSVP form when the form is re-displayed after a failed submission, leading to a Reflected Cross-Site Scripting which could be used against high-privilege users such as admins.

cna.title: WP Ghost (Hide My WP Ghost) < 7.0.19 - Unauthenticated Stored XSS via Comment Author Name

descriptions.value: The Hide My WP Ghost  WordPress plugin before 7.0.19 does not limit one of its HTML output rewriting patterns to the markup it targets, allowing unauthenticated attackers to inject HTML attributes through a comment author name that execute as Stored XSS for any visitor, including logged-in administrators, on pages that list recent comments.

cna.title: ProfilePress < 4.18.1 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation via Melange Form ID Collision

descriptions.value: The ProfilePress  WordPress plugin before 4.18.1 takes the role for an account registered through a combined login and registration form from the separate registration form that shares its numeric ID, allowing unauthenticated users to register with the elevated role, such as Editor, assigned by an unpublished registration form.

cna.title: UpdraftPlus (Free & Pro) - Unauthenticated Stored XSS via Migration Search and Replace

descriptions.value: The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 do not preserve the escaping of JSON-formatted database values when they rewrite the database during a restore to a new address or server, which could allow unauthenticated attackers to plant harmless-looking escaped markup, for example in a comment author name, that becomes Stored Cross-Site Scripting once an administrator performs such a restore.

cna.title: UpdraftPlus (Free & Pro) - Subscriber+ PHP Object Injection via Search and Replace Length Corruption

descriptions.value:
The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 do not keep serialized string lengths consistent when their database search and replace processes certain serialized values, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to plant data that becomes an attacker-chosen PHP object after an administrator runs a URL-lengthening search and replace or a migration restore.

When the replacement changes the length of the text, the declared string lengths inside the stored value no longer match and the corrupted value is written back, so when WordPress later reads it the trailing bytes are parsed as further serialized structure, including an object of a class the attacker named. No gadget chain is known in the UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 themselves; further impact depends on classes available from other installed code.

cna.title: UpdraftPlus (Free & Pro) - Subscriber+ PHP Object Injection via Search and Replace Recursion Limit

descriptions.value:
The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 do not keep a serialized value inert when their database search and replace reaches its recursion limit, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to plant data in their own user meta that is rewritten into a live PHP object when an administrator later runs a search and replace or a migration restore, and is then instantiated by WordPress on a later read.

This is distinct from CVE-2024-10957, whose fix restricted the unserialize call but left this path in place. No gadget chain is present in WordPress core or the UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 themselves; further impact depends on a suitable class from another installed UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 or .

cna.title: UpdraftPlus (Free & Pro) - Subscriber+ Privilege Escalation via Large Table Backup SQLi

descriptions.value: The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 do not safely process the output of the external database dump tool when backing up large tables, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to store profile data that turns into SQL executed when an administrator later restores the backup, for example to grant themselves the administrator role.

cna.title: UpdraftPlus (Free & Pro) - Subscriber+ PHP Object Injection via Database Restore Whitespace Trimming

descriptions.value:
The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 do not preserve long database values byte-for-byte when restoring a database backup, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to plant a serialized value that becomes a PHP Object Injection once an administrator backs up and restores the database.

No gadget chain is known in the UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 or WordPress core, so the demonstrated effect is instantiation of an attacker-chosen class in the attacker's own requests. Exploitation requires the planted data to line up exactly with how the backup is read back, which depends on details of the attacker's row and the database dump format.

cna.title: UpdraftPlus (Free & Pro) - Subscriber+ Privilege Escalation via Backup Restore Comment Discard SQLi

descriptions.value:
The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 do not correctly handle comment-like content found in the middle of a long SQL statement when restoring a database backup, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber who have stored crafted content in their own profile to have SQL executed when an administrator later restores a backup, and so escalate their account to administrator.

This is a different code path from the backup restore issue fixed in 1.26.10, and it does not depend on the database server's maximum packet size.

cna.title: Mapster WP Maps < 2.0.7 - Contributor+ Arbitrary Post, Page and Attachment Modification

descriptions.description: CWE-639 Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

affected.product: Mapster WP Maps — Mapbox, MapLibre & Google Maps for WordPress

descriptions.value: The Mapster WP Maps — Mapbox, MapLibre & Google Maps for WordPress plugin before 2.0.7 does not perform any authorization check when saving edits made through its bundled photo-gallery library, allowing any authenticated user with at least Contributor-level access to overwrite the title and content of, and write arbitrary metadata onto, any post, page or media attachment on the site regardless of ownership.
